headline: Rezoning of about 4.73 acres on Godsoe Road to urban industry district passed 9-0.
summary: The owner is FedEx Freight Inc., and the property is in the industrial area near I-95. The planning board recommended passage on November 17th, 2026. A rezoning of part of 1397 Ohio Street was referred to the planning board for its December 1st, 2026 meeting. Other approvals included a $3,048,959 WIC grant and an amendment to the KRT appraisal contract.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including a $1,015,299 aircraft deicer purchase and a $2,638,248.72 passenger facility charge application.
Referred a rezoning of part of 1397 Ohio Street and an airport funds resolve for first reading.
Approved the rezoning of a Godsoe Road property to the urban industry district, 9-0.
Approved accepting and spending $3,048,959 in state grant funds for the Women, Infants, and Children program.
Approved a special amusement permit for House of Entertainment at 128B Main Street.
Approved an amendment to the KRT appraisal contract for the property re-evaluation, with a final deadline of April 19, 2027.
discussion: WIC program grant: Members spoke in support of the program, which has a monthly average of 2,700 participants across Penobscot and Piscataquis counties. One view was that the state should handle it.
Homelessness and recovery housing: During public comment, a speaker said Bangor lost 30 people to fatal overdoses through August of this year. The speaker urged the city to put recovery first.
Minimum wage and rent control: A public speaker asked the city to set a locally raised minimum wage, like Portland's, and to adopt some form of rent control.

Sewer and housing: A public speaker said the city should invest in its sewer system and other infrastructure first. The speaker cited a 2025 city housing study that found 700-plus units are needed for households making less than $35,000 a year.

Public comment timing: Officials said public comment stays in its current place for now, and the order of meetings may change later. Residents can email daniel.carson@bangormaine.gov with their views.
